summary: This note collects creative family recipes and strategies, reported between October 2023 and May 2024, that help parents win over picky eaters. Approaches include hiding vegetables in favorite dishes, involving kids in cooking, building customizable bowls, making natural sweet treats, introducing global flavors, reinventing breakfast, and turning snacks into activities. The overall message is that creativity, patience and fun can make mealtime enjoyable and teach children about nutrition.
one_line: Parents from across the US share fun, nutritious recipes and tactics like veggie camouflage and kid participation to win over picky eaters.
key_facts: Laura Benson of Wichita, Kansas, shared her veggie camouflage strategy on October 24, 2023, including 'Mighty Mac & Cheese' with pureed butternut squash for vitamins A and C.
Laura Benson also mixes finely grated zucchini into burger patties to raise their nutritional profile.
On November 11, 2023, Miami dad Alejandro Garcia promoted 'Saturday Sushi Sessions', where his children help make rolls with avocado, cucumber and lean proteins.
Rachel Kim of Portland, Oregon, serves 'Dragon Bowls' (reported December 5, 2023): a base of brown rice or quinoa with proteins, veggies and dressings like creamy garlic-tahini or zesty ginger-soy.
The Gilbert family of Savannah, Georgia, was featured on January 10, 2024 for 'Frozen Banana Pops' dipped in dark chocolate and nuts or seeds, providing potassium, fiber and antioxidants.
Anika Patel of Fremont, California, introduced 'Tiny Tandoori Skewers' on February 21, 2024: chicken in a mild yogurt-spice marinade served with naan and cucumber-yogurt raita.
Michael Thompson, a single dad from Denver, Colorado, created the 'Breakfast Banana Split' on March 15, 2024, using Greek yogurt, fresh fruit, granola and honey instead of ice cream.

Julie Everett's 'Snacktivities' (seen April 2, 2024) from the Everett family of Phoenix, Arizona, include cutting wholegrain tortillas with cookie cutters and making art with sliced fruits and veggies.
Susan Choi of Baltimore, Maryland, shared 'Whole Food Wonders' in May 2024, such as energy balls from dates, oats and coconut, and popcorn with nutritional yeast.
The article says kids who help prepare meals feel ownership and are more likely to eat them.
Global cuisine nights are suggested as a weekly tradition that fosters appreciation for different cultures.
